# Testing a package that simd depends on makes the go command compile a test
# variant of it, and rebuild the importers it knows about against that variant.
# simd is not among them, so a rewritten package linked into the same test binary
# would see two different builds of fmt and fail to link. testing/iotest has a
# loop the wrapper would rewrite, and fmt's tests import it: it must be left
# alone here, and the test binary must link and pass.

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_DEBUG=1
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=testing/iotest
exec go test -short -run 'TestSprintf|TestScanf' -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC fmt
stdout -count=1 '^ok  	fmt	'
cmp log log.want

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
-- log.want --
skipped testing/iotest: built against a test variant of fmt
